hint.text: Commas are used to separate extra information from the rest of the sentence. There should be a comma before and after the added information.

instruction.text: Select the sentence that correctly uses punctuation for the extra information.

atoms.a: Eliza, who lives next door, is my best friend
b: ++Eliza, who lives next door, is my best friend.
Eliza who, lives next door is, my best friend.

atoms.a: The book, which was really expensive, was an original copy
b: ++The book, which was really expensive, was an original copy.
The book which, was really expensive was, an original copy.

atoms.a: The fun run, which raised lots of money for charity, was a great success.
b: ++The fun run, which raised lots of money for charity, was a great success.
The fun run which, raised lots of money, for charity was a great success.

atoms.a: My puppy, a fluffy Jack Russell, is always hungry.
b: ++My puppy, a fluffy Jack Russell, is always hungry.
My puppy a fluffy, Jack Russell is always hungry.

atoms.a: I always have Maths, my favourite subject, on a Wednesday afternoon.
b: ++I always have Maths, my favourite subject, on a Wednesday afternoon.
I always, have Maths my favourite subject on, a Wednesday afternoon.

atoms.a: Spain, where we went on holiday last year, was really hot.
b: ++Spain, where we went on holiday last year, was really hot.
Spain where, we went on holiday, last year was really hot.

instruction.text: Drag the punctuation to the correct places in the sentence.

atoms.a: My dad, who is quite sporty, plays football every week
atoms.b: My dad((,)) who is quite sporty((,)) plays football every week((.))

atoms.a: The film, set far in the future, was really hard to follow((.))
atoms.b: The film((,)) set far in the future((,)) was really hard to follow((.))

atoms.a: The snow, now falling steadily, was settling like a blanket on the ground((.))
atoms.b: The snow((,)) now falling steadily((,)) was settling like a blanket on the ground((.))
